ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit there is a 10V voltage source, with the upper end marked “+” and the lower end marked “-”. The upper-left node is connected through a 1Ω resistor to the upper-right node A. The middle branch downward from point A contains a current source labeled 5A with the arrow downward, and below it is a 4V voltage source in series, whose upper end is “+” and lower end is “-”, and it is connected to the bottom node B. The voltage U is marked on the right side, with terminal A positive and terminal B negative. Reasoning: According to the method given in the problem, take point B as the 0V reference point. Since the left 10V voltage source is positive at the top and negative at the bottom, the node potential at the left end of the 1Ω resistor is +10V. There is no external load at the A-B terminals, while the 5A current source in the middle branch draws 5A downward from point A, so according to KCL at point A, there must be 5A of current flowing through the 1Ω resistor from the left 10V node into point A. The resistor voltage drop is I R = 5A × 1Ω = 5V, so the potential at point A is 10V - 5V = 5V. Thus U_AB = V_A - V_B = 5V - 0V = 5V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the voltage U across points A and B?

method.method_draft: Set B as 0 V. From the left 10 V source, the node on the left side of the 1 Ω resistor is +10 V. Apply KCL at node A: the central current source draws 5 A downward from A, and there is no external load at A-B, so the current through the 1 Ω resistor from the 10 V node into A must be 5 A. Use Ohm's law to find the resistor drop as 5 A × 1 Ω = 5 V, hence node A is 10 V - 5 V = 5 V. Therefore U_AB = 5 V.
